War heroines still not recognised
2014-10-28T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/war-heroines-still-not-recognised-47697

Even after 43 years of independence, the supreme sacrifices made by war heroines have not been recognised.

A war heroine shared the horrors she faced in 1971, reliving the pain and suffering she went through, and carried over the years since then.

The then 13-year-old Rajia Khatun Kamala is still haunted by her experience.

Kamala, who was a resident of Kishoreganj during the Liberation War, said a razakar took her to a Pakistani military camp where she along with many others was tortured and sexually abused day after day.

Kamala could not stop her tears while sharing the darkest time of her life in her 15-minute speech in RC Majumder Arts auditorium at Dhaka University. Many of the 12 war heroines present there bowed their heads to hide their own tears.

Samajik Sahayata Udyog arranged the programme to hand over allowance to the war heroines. Kamala and 61 other war heroines receive Tk 600 from the organisation ever month as allowance.

Addressing the programme as the chief guest, Liberation War Affairs Minister AKM Mozammel Huq said the war heroines would be considered freedom fighters, but would receive more benefits than freedom fighters.

Liberation War Museum Trustee and researcher Mofidul Hoque, among others, spoke at the programme presided over by Samajik Sahayata Udyog Director Prof Abu Md Delwar Hossain.
